title: Resonance Raman spectroscopy from ab initio Hagedorn wavepacket dynamics
authors: Davide Barbiero, Léa Zupan, Jiří J. L. Vaníček
abstract: We present a practical, ab initio time-dependent method using Hagedorn wavepackets to simulate resonance Raman (RR) spectra of polyatomic molecules. Hagedorn functions---Gaussians multiplied by specific polynomials---are used to represent RR initial and final states because these functions are exact solutions to the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for at-most-quadratic potentials and can be propagated at zero cost beyond that of propagating the guiding Gaussian. Using efficient recursive formulae to compute overlaps between Hagedorn wavepackets, we can evaluate RR excitation profiles for arbitrary spectral signals, such as fundamental, overtone, combination, and hot bands. We then construct the Stokes and anti-Stokes RR spectra from these profiles. We first validate the method in a two-dimensional displaced, distorted, and Duschinsky-rotated harmonic model against numerically exact split-operator calculations. Then, we apply the method to compute RR spectra of anthracene by performing dynamics on a 66-dimensional harmonic potential energy surface constructed from density functional theory calculations.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, efficient ab initio method using Hagedorn wavepackets to simulate Resonance Raman spectra for large molecules like anthracene. By leveraging the exact solvability of Hagedorn functions in harmonic potentials, the authors compute spectra across various vibrational excitation regimes and temperatures. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for interpreting complex molecular spectroscopy.
main_problem: To simulate Resonance Raman (RR) spectra of polyatomic molecules using an ab initio time-dependent method.
main_result: The Hagedorn wavepacket method successfully computes zero- and finite-temperature RR spectra for anthracene, showing good agreement with experimental data.
method: The method uses Hagedorn wavepackets, which are exact solutions to the TDSE for quadratic potentials, to evaluate the RR cross-section via the wavepacket cross-correlation function.
model_or_system: The study focuses on polyatomic molecules, specifically anthracene, whose dynamics are modeled using a 66-dimensional harmonic potential energy surface derived from DFT calculations.
key_observables: Resonance Raman (RR) spectra (Stokes and anti-Stokes), RR excitation profiles, and the absorption spectrum.
important_parameters: Temperature (e.g., 233 K), incident/scattered wavenumbers, and the dimensionality of the potential energy surface (up to 66D).
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on the electric dipole approximation, Condon approximation, and the harmonic approximation for the potential energy surface, though the method is exact within this approximation.
figures_summary: Figures compare RR excitation profiles (quantum vs. Hagedorn) in 2D models, and show the computed RR spectrum of anthracene against experimental measurements, including comparisons with solvent effects.
paper_structure: The paper first validates the Hagedorn method in a simple 2D harmonic model against exact split-operator calculations, then applies the method to compute the full RR spectra of anthracene using DFT-derived potentials, addressing temperature and solvent effects.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly efficient, mathematically rigorous quantum dynamics tool (Hagedorn wavepackets) for calculating complex spectroscopic signals in molecular systems, bridging quantum chemistry calculations with observable spectroscopic data.
